title: Title and 1st Point: Discipline and Gratitude Lesson for the Commanding Self

questions.question: What does the speaker call his own nafs at the start?
questions.answer: Foolish.

questions.question: What are some things this nafs loves too much?
questions.answer: Glory, fame, praise, and thinking too much of itself.

questions.question: What example shows that a tiny beginning can be linked to many fruits?
questions.answer: A small seed connected to a fig tree with many figs.

questions.question: What other example is given about many fruits growing from something weak-looking?
questions.answer: Grapes growing on a dry vine branch.

questions.question: If the branch and seed truly made the fruits by themselves, what might they think they deserve?
questions.answer: Praise and honor.

questions.question: Why is the nafs told it should not be proud of blessings?
questions.answer: Because it is not the real maker of them.

questions.question: What part of a person makes the nafs more blameworthy than a seed or branch?
questions.answer: It has a choice, or will.

questions.question: What does pride do to blessings, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It lowers their value.

questions.question: What does thanklessness do to blessings?
questions.answer: It wipes them out.

questions.question: What wrong happens when someone claims blessings as his own?
questions.answer: He takes what is not truly his.

questions.question: What should a person do instead of showing off his deeds?
questions.answer: Thank Allah.

questions.question: What should a person have instead of wanting fame?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What should a person seek instead of praise?
questions.answer: Repentance and forgiveness.

questions.question: Where is a person’s real perfection found?
questions.answer: In knowing Allah, not in being self-centered.

questions.question: What is the nafs compared to in the world?
questions.answer: Nature.

questions.question: In this comparison, what do both the nafs and nature receive?
questions.answer: Good is given to them, and evil is connected to them.

questions.question: Are the nafs and nature described as active makers or receivers?
questions.answer: Receivers.

questions.question: What kind of effect are they said to have?
questions.answer: They can become a reason for evil.

questions.question: Why were they made as veils?
questions.answer: So ugly-looking things could be linked to them, while Allah is known to be free from defect.

questions.question: What big mistake happens when the nafs acts like a partner with its Creator?
questions.answer: It becomes very foolish and does a great wrong.

questions.question: Why should the nafs not say, “Beauty appears through me, so I am beautiful”?
questions.answer: Because beauty only passes through it; it does not become its own.

questions.question: Why should the nafs not say, “I was chosen, so I must be better”?
questions.answer: Because those gifts were given to it out of need, weakness, and poverty before Allah.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to in this passage?
questions.answer: The speaker’s own nafs.

questions.question: What bad habits of the nafs are named near the beginning?
questions.answer: Loving attention, wanting praise, and being full of ego.

questions.question: What plant example is used to teach about where fruit really comes from?
questions.answer: A fig tree growing from a tiny seed.

questions.question: What vine example is also used?
questions.answer: Many grape bunches hanging from a dry branch.

questions.question: What lesson do these plant examples help teach?
questions.answer: Something can carry blessings without being their true owner or maker.

questions.question: Does the passage say the nafs truly produces blessings by itself?
questions.answer: No, it does not.

questions.question: Why does the nafs deserve blame instead of pride?
questions.answer: Because it misuses blessings with pride and wrong claims.

questions.question: How does conceit affect blessings?
questions.answer: It ruins them.

questions.question: How does being ungrateful affect blessings?
questions.answer: It makes them count for nothing.

questions.question: What is the right response to blessings?
questions.answer: Thanking Allah.

questions.question: What is better for a believer than fame?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What is better for a believer than being praised?
questions.answer: Saying sorry to Allah and asking His forgiveness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes a person truly complete?
questions.answer: Recognizing Allah.

questions.question: What in the world is like the nafs in the body?
questions.answer: Nature in the world.

questions.question: What do the nafs and nature have in common?
questions.answer: They receive good but are where evil is linked.

questions.question: What does it mean that they are passive?
questions.answer: They are not the real source and do not create by themselves.

questions.question: Why can they be connected with evil?
questions.answer: Because they fail to receive good in the right way.

questions.question: What is one purpose of making them a covering or veil?
questions.answer: To keep people from wrongly thinking Allah has defects.

questions.question: What false idea is rejected about being a place where beauty appears?
questions.answer: That this makes the person beautiful by himself.

questions.question: What is the better way to think about gifts shown through a person?
questions.answer: They are given by Allah, not proof that the person is great.

questions.question: What three words describe why those gifts were given first to that person?
questions.answer: More poor, more needy, and more sad.

questions.question: What main warning does this passage give about the nafs?
questions.answer: Do not let it become proud and steal credit from Allah.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly correcting in the nafs?
questions.answer: Its pride and self-love.

questions.question: What are the two fruit examples used in the passage?
questions.answer: Figs from a seed and grapes on a vine branch.

questions.question: Why are those examples important?
questions.answer: They show that carrying something good is not the same as creating it.

questions.question: When people enjoy fruit, who might they wrongly praise in the example?
questions.answer: The branch or the seed.

questions.question: What similar mistake can the nafs make?
questions.answer: It can think blessings belong to it.

questions.question: Why is the nafs even less excused than a branch or seed?
questions.answer: Because it has will and choice.

questions.question: What happens to blessings when pride enters?
questions.answer: Their worth goes down.

questions.question: What happens to blessings when a person is thankful or unthankful?
questions.answer: Thankfulness keeps them right, but unthankfulness cancels them.

questions.question: What does the passage say about taking ownership of blessings?
questions.answer: It is like taking what is not lawfully yours.

questions.question: Name one thing the nafs should do with blessings.
questions.answer: Thank Allah.

questions.question: Name one character trait the nafs should have.
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: Name one spiritual act the nafs should do after mistakes.
questions.answer: Repent and ask forgiveness.

questions.question: What should a person know instead of being centered on himself?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say the nafs is like inside the body?
questions.answer: Like nature in the world.

questions.question: What is not the job of the nafs or nature?
questions.answer: Being the true doer and source.

questions.question: What role do they have instead?
questions.answer: They receive things and can be blamed when evil appears.

questions.question: Why are ugly-looking things sometimes linked to them?
questions.answer: So Allah is known to be perfect and free of defect.

questions.question: What opposite path did the nafs take from its true job?
questions.answer: It acted as if it shared in Allah’s work.

questions.question: What does the passage call a person who worships himself and nature?
questions.answer: Extremely foolish and deeply unjust.

questions.question: Why is “beauty shows in me, so I am beautiful” a wrong thought?
questions.answer: Because beauty passes through without becoming the person’s own.

questions.question: Why is “I was chosen, so I have special merit” also rejected?
questions.answer: Because Allah gave those gifts due to the person’s need, not due to greatness.

questions.question: What feeling should this passage build in a Muslim child’s heart?
questions.answer: Thankfulness to Allah and a humble heart.

questions.question: What kind of inner part is being scolded in this passage?
questions.answer: The nafs.

questions.question: What does the nafs enjoy that can be dangerous?
questions.answer: Being honored and praised.

questions.question: What first nature example is used to explain the lesson?
questions.answer: A tiny seed connected to a tree full of figs.

questions.question: What second nature example is used?
questions.answer: A vine branch with many bunches of grapes.

questions.question: If someone praised the branch as if it made the grapes by itself, what would be wrong with that?
questions.answer: The branch is not the true maker.

questions.question: What is the same wrong idea when a person boasts about blessings?
questions.answer: He acts like he made them himself.

questions.question: How does free choice make the nafs responsible?
questions.answer: It can choose pride and misuse what was given.

questions.question: What does the passage say pride does to blessings?
questions.answer: It makes them less valuable.

questions.question: What does claiming blessings as your own do?
questions.answer: It becomes an unfair taking.

questions.question: What should come from a believer after receiving blessings?
questions.answer: Thanks to Allah.

questions.question: What attitude should replace wanting attention?
questions.answer: Humbleness.

questions.question: What should replace wanting people’s praise?
questions.answer: Repenting and asking Allah to forgive.

questions.question: What is better than thinking only about yourself?
questions.answer: Knowing and recognizing Allah.

questions.question: What thing in the outside world is like the nafs?
questions.answer: Nature.

questions.question: What are both nature and the nafs said to be, not the source but what?
questions.answer: The receivers.

questions.question: What one bad effect can come from them?
questions.answer: Evil can be connected to them.

questions.question: Why were they made as a kind of cover?
questions.answer: To carry the blame for what seems ugly, while Allah is above all fault.

questions.question: What serious error happens when the nafs forgets this job?
questions.answer: It behaves as if it were Allah’s partner.

questions.question: What two wrong kinds of worship are mentioned?
questions.answer: Worshiping the self and worshiping nature.

questions.question: Why is it wrong to think that showing beauty means you own beauty?
questions.answer: Because you only pass it along.

questions.question: What is the answer to the thought, “People chose me, so I must be special”?
questions.answer: No; the gifts came because of greater need.

questions.question: According to the end of the passage, what conditions of a person can come before being given gifts?
questions.answer: Being poor, needy, and sad.

questions.question: What is one word that describes the nafs in this passage?
questions.answer: Proud.

questions.question: What does the nafs want from other people?
questions.answer: Praise.

questions.question: What tree fruit is used as an example?
questions.answer: Figs.

questions.question: What vine fruit is used as another example?
questions.answer: Grapes.

questions.question: Do those examples teach that the seed and branch are fully in charge?
questions.answer: No, they do not.

questions.question: What do those examples help us understand about people and blessings?
questions.answer: People may carry blessings, but Allah gives them.

questions.question: Why should the nafs be corrected again and again?
questions.answer: Because it keeps becoming proud and ungrateful.

questions.question: What does pride do to a blessing?
questions.answer: It reduces its worth.

questions.question: What does ingratitude do to a blessing?
questions.answer: It makes it empty and lost.

questions.question: If someone says, “This blessing is mine because I made it,” what is wrong with that?
questions.answer: It is a false claim.

questions.question: What is the proper duty of a servant of Allah after doing good?
questions.answer: To thank Allah, not boast.

questions.question: Which is the better quality: fame or humility?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: Which is the better path: praise or repentance?
questions.answer: Repentance.

questions.question: Where does true excellence come from?
questions.answer: From recognizing Allah.

questions.question: What is the nafs compared with to teach another lesson?
questions.answer: Nature.

questions.question: In that lesson, are the nafs and nature creators or receivers?
questions.answer: Receivers.

questions.question: What kind of things are assigned to them so Allah is known as perfect?
questions.answer: Things that seem ugly or faulty.

questions.question: What happens when the nafs turns good into evil through weakness?
questions.answer: It goes against its real purpose.

questions.question: What is so bad about acting like a partner with the Creator?
questions.answer: It is a huge wrong and great foolishness.

questions.question: Why is being a place where beauty appears not a reason to brag?
questions.answer: Because the beauty is not your own.

questions.question: Why are good works shown through some people first?
questions.answer: Because they may be more needy before Allah.

questions.question: What message should a Muslim student remember from this passage?
questions.answer: Be humble, thank Allah, and never steal credit from Him.

questions.question: At the beginning, what kind of nafs is being addressed?
questions.answer: One that loves praise and honor.

questions.question: What does the passage use from nature to teach about blessings?
questions.answer: A seed, a fig tree, a vine branch, and grapes.

questions.question: What do these examples show about the real owner of good things?
questions.answer: The one carrying them is not the true owner.

questions.question: If the nafs were like the seed in the wrong way, what would it start to think?
questions.answer: That it deserves pride for the blessings.

questions.question: Why is that thought corrected right away?
questions.answer: Because the nafs does not truly make those blessings.

questions.question: What special power makes the nafs answerable for its behavior?
questions.answer: The power to choose.

questions.question: What effect does arrogance have on the gifts a person receives?
questions.answer: It lowers and spoils them.

questions.question: What effect does not thanking Allah have?
questions.answer: It removes the good of the blessings.

questions.question: What does the passage compare wrong ownership claims to?
questions.answer: Taking something unlawfully.

questions.question: What should be done with blessings instead of boasting?
questions.answer: Thank Allah for them.

questions.question: What heart quality should replace the love of fame?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What action should replace the wish for people’s praise?
questions.answer: Seeking forgiveness.

questions.question: What understanding should replace self-centeredness?
questions.answer: Recognizing Allah.

questions.question: What is the nafs said to resemble in the larger world?
questions.answer: Nature.

questions.question: What shared job do the nafs and nature have?
questions.answer: They receive good and are where evil is attributed.

questions.question: Why are they not called the real source?
questions.answer: Because they do not create independently.

questions.question: Why is a veil needed in this teaching?
questions.answer: So things that look ugly can be assigned there, while Allah’s perfection is protected in our understanding.

questions.question: What wrong turn did the nafs take away from its natural duty?
questions.answer: It began acting as if it shared Allah’s work.

questions.question: What judgment is given about worshiping oneself or nature?
questions.answer: It is foolish and a great injustice.

questions.question: Why is the sentence about beauty appearing through a person not enough to prove merit?
questions.answer: Because passing beauty on is not the same as owning it.

questions.question: What answer is given to the thought, “I was picked, so I must be better than others”?
questions.answer: Gifts may come first to the one who is more needy.

questions.question: What three feelings should this passage teach us to have before Allah?
questions.answer: Humility, thankfulness, and repentance.
